title: A solid holds its shape, and that shape fixes its volume
summary: A solid holds its shape, and the volume of a solid is fixed by that shape.
body: NASA Glenn says the molecules in a solid are closely bound to one another by molecular forces. A solid holds its shape, and the volume of a solid is fixed by the shape of the solid. A liquid, which borrows the outline of a holder, is a different claim. The page does not rank materials from hard to soft, and it does not say a solid can be poured.

sources.title: States of Matter
sources.author: NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.note: NASA Glenn Beginner's Guide to Propulsion, U.S. government work, public domain. Page last updated 13 May 2021. Supports a solid holding its shape, with volume fixed by that shape.
